title: CHEM1A Practice Quiz — Objective 1: Foundations (DRAFT pending Gilley approval)

items.stem: Filtered air (no dust or droplets) is best classified as:
choices: A compound, because it contains nitrogen and oxygen
items.explain: Air is uniform throughout but its components are not chemically bonded — homogeneous mixture. Calling it a compound is the classic misconception.

items.stem: Which sample is a pure compound?
items.explain: Sucrose has one fixed composition of C, H, O. Stainless steel and ocean water are mixtures; diamond is an element (carbon).

items.stem: Which is a chemical property of magnesium?
choices: It burns in air with a bright white flame
items.explain: Burning changes the identity (magnesium oxide forms). Color, conductivity, and melting point leave the identity unchanged — physical.

items.stem: Dissolving salt in water is a physical change because:
choices: A new substance with new properties forms
The salt can be recovered unchanged by evaporating the water
Energy is absorbed during the process
items.explain: Recoverability shows the identity never changed. Energy flow and homogeneity happen in both physical and chemical changes — those distractors test the real misconceptions.

items.stem: The prefix centi- means:
items.explain: Centi = 10 to the minus 2 (one hundredth). Deci is one tenth; milli is one thousandth.

items.stem: Grams per cubic centimeter is an example of:
items.explain: It is built from two units (mass over length cubed) — derived. The base units are things like kilogram, meter, second.

items.stem: How many significant figures are in 0.0808 grams?
items.explain: Leading zeros never count; the captive zero does: 8, 0, 8 = three.

items.stem: The product 4.56 centimeters x 1.4 centimeters, reported correctly, is:
items.explain: Multiplication keeps the fewest significant figures (two, from 1.4): 6.4. Reporting 6.384 is the calculator-copy misconception.

items.stem: A balance gives 4 readings of the same 10.00 gram standard: 8.51, 8.50, 8.52, 8.51 grams. The balance is:
items.explain: Tightly clustered (precise) but far from the true value (not accurate) — likely a systematic error like miscalibration.

items.stem: Random error, as opposed to systematic error, tends to:
choices: Shift every measurement in the same direction
Scatter measurements around the true value in both directions
Disappear when the instrument is recalibrated
items.explain: Random error scatters both ways; systematic error biases one way and is the one recalibration can fix.

items.stem: A board is 3.00 feet long. Its length in centimeters (1 foot = 12 inches, 1 inch = 2.54 centimeters) is:
items.explain: 3.00 x 12 x 2.54 = 91.4 centimeters. The 7.62 distractor skipped the feet-to-inches step; 36.0 stopped at inches; 1.18 divided instead of multiplied.

items.stem: To convert 0.75 liters to milliliters, the correct setup is:
items.explain: The factor must put liters on the bottom so they cancel: 1000 milliliters per 1 liter. The others orient the factor upside down — the number one dimensional-analysis error.

items.stem: Mercury's density is 13.6 grams per milliliter. The mass of 5.00 milliliters of mercury is:
items.explain: Density works as a conversion factor: 5.00 mL x 13.6 g/mL = 68.0 g. The 0.368 distractor divided; 18.6 added; 2.72 inverted.

items.stem: A 15.8 gram object displaces 2.0 milliliters of water. Its density, correctly reported, is:
items.explain: 15.8 / 2.0 = 7.9 — two significant figures, controlled by 2.0. Reporting 7.90 over-claims precision; that distractor is the sig-fig overlay trap.

items.stem: The ion 27-Al-3+ (aluminum-27, charge 3+) contains:
items.explain: Protons = 13; neutrons = 27 - 13 = 14; electrons = 13 - 3 = 10. Adding electrons for a positive ion is the sign-error misconception.

items.stem: An ion has 17 protons, 20 neutrons, and 18 electrons. It is:
items.explain: 17 protons = chlorine; mass number = 17 + 20 = 37; one extra electron = 1- charge. The 38-Ar distractor counts electrons as protons; the 17-Cl distractor confuses atomic number with mass number.

items.stem: Lithium is 7.59 percent lithium-6 (6.015 u) and 92.41 percent lithium-7 (7.016 u). Its average atomic mass is closest to:
items.explain: (6.015)(0.0759) + (7.016)(0.9241) = 6.94. The 6.50 distractor is the unweighted average — the central misconception this tag exists to kill.

items.stem: An element's average atomic mass is 121.76 u. It has two isotopes, masses 120.90 u and 122.90 u. Which must be true?
choices: The two isotopes are equally abundant
The isotope with mass 120.90 u is more abundant
The isotope with mass 122.90 u is more abundant
The average is impossible for these isotopes
items.explain: 121.76 sits closer to 120.90, so that isotope dominates the weighted average. Reasoning from the position of the average IS the reverse-direction skill the final exam tests.

items.stem: The element in Group 1, Period 4 is:
items.explain: Period 4, first column = potassium. Sodium is Period 3 — the row-versus-column mix-up is the targeted error.

items.stem: Which element is a metalloid?
items.explain: Silicon sits on the staircase line. Sulfur is a nonmetal; silver and strontium are metals. All four start with S on purpose — classify by position, not by name.

items.stem: A well-tested explanation of WHY a natural pattern occurs is called a:
items.explain: Theory explains why; law summarizes the observed pattern; hypothesis is the tentative starting explanation.

items.stem: The mass number of an atom equals:
choices: The number of protons plus neutrons
The weighted average of the isotope masses
items.explain: Mass number A = protons + neutrons, a whole-number count for one atom. The weighted average is the atomic mass on the periodic table — the distractor most students pick.
